title: Problem solving core: data structures and algorithms
goal: Build the algorithmic toolbox that interviews and contests still test: complexity reasoning, arrays and hashing, sorting and binary search, stacks, recursion, bitmasks and greedy.

steps.title: Pattern library
steps.note: Use it after each problem: name the signal that points to the technique.

steps.title: Algorithm templates
steps.note: Read, retype from memory, then adapt. Do not just paste.

steps.title: Competitive Programmer's Handbook (Antti Laaksonen)
steps.note: A free, concise companion to this track.

steps.title: CSES Problem Set
steps.note: Work through Introductory, Sorting and Searching, then Dynamic Programming and Graph sections in order.

steps.title: cp-algorithms
steps.note: Reference for every algorithm that appears later.

steps.title: Graphs, shortest paths, DSU/MST and dynamic programming
steps.note: These modules (CP 11 to 14) are not written on this site yet. Use the CSES graph and DP sections with cp-algorithms until they are.

exit: You have finished the CSES Introductory and Sorting and Searching sections.
You reach about 1200 on Codeforces in rated or virtual contests.
You can solve a medium problem in 45 minutes without hints and explain its complexity.
You can name the technique for a new problem from its signals and constraints before coding.
